note: Labels and plain lines for replays, curated from the experiments' own documents. The adapter copies an experiment's entry into the catalogue and copies from a run only the parameters and readouts named here. A replay shows what the run recorded and never computes a verdict of its own. Only the experiments whose entry says listed stand in the page's list (decided on 17 November 2026: the replication and GARD, which `doors` names and which opens its own view); the others are packaged for the checks and never exported, and the runs a species names (the planarian's looping run) are published unlisted.

gap-junction-linear-network.units: The two forms state [mR] in their own units: the Norton form's runs in mM, the as-written runs in µM (in each, the preprint's scaled unit is one of them). The page never converts one to the other.
gap-junction-linear-network.label: Gap-junction networks of a linear model, after Grodstein, Mathews and Levin (2026)
gap-junction-linear-network.plain: How strongly must gap junctions couple cells for healthy tissue to turn a tumor back to the healthy state, and how do the tumor's membrane voltage and connexin expression change that? The preprint's linear model of cells joined by gap junctions (its equations 1-2 and Figures 3, 5 and 8) run on Cells' engine: J. Grodstein, J. Mathews and M. Levin, "Membrane voltage and connexin expression work together to enhance tumor growth and metastasis in cancer", bioRxiv, 2026, doi:10.64898/2026.09.02.748840 (v1, CC BY 4.0). Each arm is one network of the figures: two cells, Figure 5a's seven, or a chain, at one coupling.

outcome.text: The preprint's linear model ("intuitive model": equations 1-2, appendix, Figures 3, 5 and 8) runs on the engine in two forms: as written, and as its exact Norton equivalent on @3's own routes, which is the check on the as-written runs. The preprint's tissue simulations (Tables 1-3) are not run here: they need four engine features, which the lead filed as FR-15 to FR-17. One tissue condition runs on today's engine: the "neither" condition on the 1D line.

gap-junction-tissue-line.label: The tissue line: 25 cells, the first six a tumor, at four strengths of coupling
gap-junction-tissue-line.plain: One tissue condition of the example runs on the engine: a line of 25 touching cells, the first six a tumor, where each cell runs the EMT switch (miR200, Zeb mRNA and ZEB) and only miR200 crosses the gap junctions, at one junction diffusion constant D for each run. Four runs, recorded densely: D = 0, and three values of D fixed before they ran, at half, once and twice the threshold the search reported; none was refused. Each cell is coloured by its miR200 minus Zeb mRNA, as the experiment's driver states it beside each run.

says: Four runs: D = 0, and three fixed before they ran at half, once and twice the threshold the search reported (x2/2 below, x2 near, 2 x2 above), recorded densely; none was refused.

Its threshold, from the search rerun after an engine fix (FR-19): 7.1777e-15 m²/s. The search was a comparison with BITSEY's log saved at b2cb370, written by an earlier revision of its code: Cells' threshold is 0.99968 of the logged value, inside the band fixed before the run; development, not judged.
BITSEY is the preprint's authors' public code and logs: it was not run, and its code is never copied into Cells.

gap-junction-tissue-sheet.label: Cells' extension: a tissue sheet of 9 by 9 cells, a 3 by 3 tumor in the middle, at six strengths of coupling
gap-junction-tissue-sheet.plain: Cells' extension of the example, not part of the replication: 9 by 9 touching cells with junctions to their four neighbours and a 3 by 3 tumor patch in the middle, with the line's switch, seeds and uncoupled 500 s, at six values of the junction diffusion constant D, with x2 the line's threshold. Each cell is coloured by its miR200 minus Zeb mRNA, as the experiment's driver states it beside each run.

says: The sheet is an extension beyond the replication, not part of it. Its coupled horizon is 2,000 s, a tenth of the line's, so each outcome is the state at 2,000 s.

So, at 2,000 s, the sheet's threshold lies between x2/8 and x2/4 (9.0e-16 to 1.8e-15 m²/s), four to eight times below the line's x2. That is observed, at the sheet's shorter horizon; why it is lower is not measured here.

e07-v1.label: E07-v1: renewal
e07-v1.plain: Can a voltage pattern written into a tissue survive while its cells are replaced? A disc of cells sits at a depolarised voltage (D) in a sheet of 127 cells at their resting voltage (H). Cells are then replaced one at a time by a copy of a neighbour, and each run is compared with plain copying on the same schedule.

outcome.label: The disc did not renew
outcome.text: Under donor-copy turnover the written disc did not renew, and the coupling's effect was far smaller than predicted. 8 of 15 scored predictions held.

all_h.label: Stopped early: every cell had fallen to H

control.label: Control: disc only
control.plain: Only the disc's cells are replaced, each by a copy of a neighbour inside the disc. Under plain copying the pattern passes by construction, so the control isolates the electrical loss of D copies.

fast k1.label: Inheritance route, fast k1
fast k1.plain: Cells across the whole sheet are replaced by copies of a neighbour, drawn blind to its state. Each cell stays 17 minutes before it is replaced.

central k1.label: Inheritance route, central k1
central k1.plain: Cells across the whole sheet are replaced by copies of a neighbour, drawn blind to its state. Each cell stays 40 minutes before it is replaced.

fast k3.label: Inheritance route, fast k3
fast k3.plain: Cells across the whole sheet are replaced by copies of a neighbour, drawn blind to its state. Each cell stays 51 minutes before it is replaced.

threshold-finding.label: Boundary set
threshold-finding.plain: Isolated newcomers with fast junction formation: how fast must junctions form for a newcomer to be recruited into the written state?

classes.label: Neutral
classes.description: At the judged record: |ΔJ| ≤ δ, D-loss ≤ 2% and recruitment ≤ 2%.

classes.label: Erosion
classes.description: At the judged record: ΔJ < −δ or D-loss > 5%, and not recruitment.

classes.label: Recruitment
classes.description: At the judged record: ΔJ > +δ or recruitment > 5%, and not erosion.

classes.label: Mixed
classes.description: Both the erosion and the recruitment conditions hold.

classes.label: Small bias
classes.description: Anything else: none of the other classes holds.

e07-v1.class_note: The class is the one the experiment's own summary records for this run, judged at its judged record against the paired copy-only null.

heredity-turnover-literature.label: Turnover pre-screen: the literature newcomer rule
heredity-turnover-literature.plain: A development run before E07-v1: can a voltage pattern written into a tissue renew itself when its cells are replaced the way the literature describes? A disc of cells sits at a depolarised voltage (D) in a sheet of 127 cells at their resting voltage (H). Only the disc's cells are replaced, the oldest first. A newcomer arrives with no junctions and forms them over tens of minutes; it is either a fresh cell at the resting voltage or a copy of a neighbour. Each run starts two minutes after a brief cue wrote the disc.

iso.plain: Each replaced cell's place is taken by a fresh cell at the resting voltage (H). It arrives with no junctions to its neighbours and forms them after a lag, over tens of minutes.

donor.plain: Each replaced cell's place is taken by a copy of one of its neighbours, drawn at random from inside or outside the disc: the neighbour divides into the place. The copy arrives with no junctions and forms them after a lag, over tens of minutes.

heredity-pilot-w1.label: W1: heredity pilot
heredity-pilot-w1.plain: A development pilot before E07-v1: can a brief cue write a voltage pattern into a tissue? The tissue has 225 cells, all at their resting voltage (H). For two seconds an added sodium leak opens in the cells of a disc of 19 or 37 cells. The replays show these two runs on the full tissue: one second before the cue, the cue, and three seconds after it. The pilot's 70-minute runs, in which five of six written discs held, used a simpler sheet of 127 cells and are not among the replays.

planarian-loop.label: Planarian loop (development run)
planarian-loop.plain: A development run of the engine, not judged: FR-11's interim planarian loop. Seven planarian heredity cells on a hexagonal patch, with a subthreshold square-wave current into the centre cell (cell_3), run for four periods and then saved for one more period of 2 s, packaged to loop. An illustration at a low level of detail: lumped cells and reduced laws, with the cells' places prescribed by its builder. It is not a measurement of a planarian, and it shows no result.
